claim: Dynamic Ca2+ signals reflect acute changes in membrane excitability and mediate signaling cascades in chronic processes.
source: Dynamic Ca2+ signals reflect acute changes in membrane excitability, and also mediate signaling cascades in chronic processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about Ca2+ signaling that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Chronic Ca2+ imaging is challenged by the cytotoxicity intrinsic to calmodulin (CaM)-based GCaMP.
source: In both cases, chronic Ca2+ imaging is often desired, but challenged by the cytotoxicity intrinsic to calmodulin (CaM)-based GCaMP, a series of genetically-encoded Ca2+ indicators that have been widely applied.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental data and observations presented throughout the manuscript showing GCaMP toxicity.

claim: GCaMP-X is designed to eliminate unwanted interactions between conventional GCaMP and endogenous (apo)CaM-binding proteins.
source: Here, we demonstrate the performance of GCaMP-X in chronic Ca2+ imaging of cortical neurons, where GCaMP-X by design is to eliminate the unwanted interactions between the conventional GCaMP and endogenous (apo)CaM-binding proteins.
evidence: This describes the design principle of GCaMP-X, which is validated by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: GCaMP-X showed less damage and improved performance in two-photon imaging compared to GCaMP when expressed at high levels over an extended time frame in adult mice.
source: By expressing in adult mice at high levels over an extended time frame, GCaMP-X showed less damage and improved performance in two-photon imaging of sensory (whisker-deflection) responses or spontaneous Ca2+ fluctuations, in comparison with GCaMP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vivo imaging experiments comparing GCaMP and GCaMP-X.

claim: Chronic Ca2+ imaging of one month or longer was conducted for cultured cortical neurons expressing GCaMP-X.
source: Chronic Ca2+ imaging of one month or longer was conducted for cultured cortical neurons expressing GCaMP-X, unveiling that spontaneous/local Ca2+ transients progressively developed into autonomous/global Ca2+ oscillations.
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental data presented in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Spontaneous/local Ca2+ transients progressively developed into autonomous/global Ca2+ oscillations in cultured cortical neurons expressing GCaMP-X.
source: Chronic Ca2+ imaging of one month or longer was conducted for cultured cortical neurons expressing GCaMP-X, unveiling that spontaneous/local Ca2+ transients progressively developed into autonomous/global Ca2+ oscillations.
evidence: This observation is supported by the longitudinal Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Dysregulations of both neuritogenesis and Ca2+ oscillations became discernible around 2–3 weeks after virus injection or drug induction to express GCaMP in newborn or mature neurons.
source: Dysregulations of both neuritogenesis and Ca2+ oscillations became discernible around 2–3 weeks after virus injection or drug induction to express GCaMP in newborn or mature neurons, which were exacerbated by stronger or prolonged expression of GCaMP.
evidence: This is supported by the temporal analysis of neurite length and Ca2+ oscillation parameters shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Dysregulations caused by GCaMP were exacerbated by stronger or prolonged expression.
source: Dysregulations of both neuritogenesis and Ca2+ oscillations became discernible around 2–3 weeks after virus injection or drug induction to express GCaMP in newborn or mature neurons, which were exacerbated by stronger or prolonged expression of GCaMP.
evidence: This is supported by dose-dependent and time-dependent experiments shown in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Neurons expressing GCaMP-X were significantly less damaged or perturbed compared to those expressing GCaMP.
source: In contrast, neurons expressing GCaMP-X were significantly less damaged or perturbed, altogether highlighting the unique importance of oscillatory Ca2+ to neural development and neuronal health.
evidence: This is supported by comparative data throughout the manuscript showing better morphological and functional outcomes with GCaMP-X.

claim: Ca2+ signals play pivotal roles in the brain, closely involved in membrane excitability, sensory transduction, synaptic transmission, neural development, and plasticity.
source: Ca2+ signals play pivotal roles in the brain, closely involved in membrane excitability, sensory transduction, synaptic transmission, neural development, and plasticity (Berridge et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Ca2+ dysregulations are linked with mental disorders including Parkinson's diseases, Alzheimer's diseases, epilepsy, and schizophrenia.
source: Ca2+ dysregulations are linked with the mental disorders including Parkinson's diseases, Alzheimer's diseases, epilepsy, and schizophrenia (Chan et al., 2007; Fernández de Sevilla et al., 2006; Khan et al., 2020; Liebscher et al., 2016), suggesting that multiple factors and cascades may converge to Ca2+ as one of the central factors underlying brain diseases, referred as the calcium hypothesis (Berridge, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Multiple factors and cascades may converge to Ca2+ as one of the central factors underlying brain diseases, referred to as the calcium hypothesis.
source: Ca2+ dysregulations are linked with the mental disorders including Parkinson's diseases, Alzheimer's diseases, epilepsy, and schizophrenia (Chan et al., 2007; Fernández de Sevilla et al., 2006; Khan et al., 2020; Liebscher et al., 2016), suggesting that multiple factors and cascades may converge to Ca2+ as one of the central factors underlying brain diseases, referred as the calcium hypothesis (Berridge, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Berridge, 2010.

claim: Cellular Ca2+ signals can be categorized as genomic versus non-genomic based on their downstream consequences.
source: According to their downstream consequences, cellular Ca2+ signals could be categorized as genomic versus non-genomic, to reflect the fact that in some cases where gene expressions are regulated (chronic) versus in other cases only the (acute) functions of existing proteins are concerned.
evidence: This is a conceptual framework based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cellular Ca2+ reflects single-neuron activities, such as spontaneous fluctuations and stimulus-evoked responses.
source: Acutely, cellular Ca2+ reflects single-neuron activities, such as spontaneous fluctuations and stimulus-evoked responses (Chen et al., 2013; O'Banion and Yasuda, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators (GECIs) represented by GCaMP have been broadly applied to monitor neurons and other excitable cells.
source: In fact, genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators (GECIs) represented by GCaMP, based on CaM (calmodulin) and Ca2+/CaM-binding motif M13, have been broadly applied to monitor neurons and other excitable cells (Akerboom et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Dana et al., 2019; Nakai et al., 2001; Tallini et al., 2006; Tian et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: GCaMP is based on CaM (calmodulin) and Ca2+/CaM-binding motif M13.
source: In fact, genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators (GECIs) represented by GCaMP, based on CaM (calmodulin) and Ca2+/CaM-binding motif M13, have been broadly applied to monitor neurons and other excitable cells (Akerboom et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Dana et al., 2019; Nakai et al., 2001; Tallini et al., 2006; Tian et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the molecular design of GCaMP, which is established knowledge.

claim: Ca2+ is tightly coupled to various chronic effects or processes, including Ca2+-dependent gene transcription and expression, neurite outgrowth or pruning, long-term potentiation or depression, learning and memory, and neural degeneration.
source: In addition to a faithful index of acute responses (in the timescale of seconds/minutes, such as a burst of action potentials), Ca2+ is often tightly coupled to various chronic effects or processes, for example, Ca2+-dependent gene transcription and expression, neurite outgrowth or pruning, long-term potentiation or depression, learning and memory, and neural degeneration (O'Banion and Yasuda, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: It is highly desirable to monitor long-term Ca2+ dynamics (days/weeks or longer) for cells, tissues, organs, or even whole organisms.
source: Therefore, it is highly desirable to monitor the long-term Ca2+ dynamics (days/weeks or longer) for cells, tissues, organs, or even whole organisms, which would greatly facilitate mechanistic understanding of the genomic/chronic roles of Ca2+ in diverse pathophysiology (Garcia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the need for chronic Ca2+ imaging, supported by a citation.

claim: GECIs hold great promise to avoid chronic immune responses and recording instability that electrodes are often encountered with.
source: GECIs hold great promise to avoid chronic immune responses and recoding instability that electrodes are often encountered with (Aramuni and Griesbeck, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: GCaMP and other GECIs have been demonstrated as more advantageous methods over electrodes or dyes during chronic imaging of neurons.
source: Indeed, GCaMP and other GECIs have been demonstrated as more advantageous methods over electrodes or dyes during chronic imaging of neurons (Aoki et al., 2017; Murphy et al., 2020; Tian et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Neural toxicities often accompany long-term expression of GCaMP or chronic GCaMP imaging with either virus infected or transgenic neurons.
source: Unfortunately, neural toxicities often accompany long-term expression of GCaMP or chronic GCaMP imaging with either virus infected (Chen et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2018) or transgenic neurons (Steinmetz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GCaMP indicators cause side-effects in neurons by perturbing L-type CaV1 channels and presumably other (apo)CaM-binding proteins.
source: Perturbing L-type CaV1 channels and presumably other (apo)CaM-binding proteins, GCaMP indicators cause side-effects in neurons which have been documented especially for enhanced or prolonged expressions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the manuscript, particularly the electrophysiology experiments in Figure 1E.

claim: jGCaMP7b accumulated into the nuclei in a substantial subpopulation of cortical neurons indexed by N/C (nucleus/cytosol) ratio.
source: Following the protocol of transient transfection (Figure 1A), jGCaMP7b accumulated into the nuclei in a substantial subpopulation of cortical neurons indexed by N/C (nucleus/cytosol) ratio (Figure 1B), considered as the hallmark of GCaMP side-effects.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Nuclear accumulation is considered as the hallmark of GCaMP side-effects.
source: Following the protocol of transient transfection (Figure 1A), jGCaMP7b accumulated into the nuclei in a substantial subpopulation of cortical neurons indexed by N/C (nucleus/cytosol) ratio (Figure 1B), considered as the hallmark of GCaMP side-effects.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on observations throughout the manuscript.

claim: jGCaMP7b exhibited even more severe nuclear accumulation than other GCaMP variants.
source: Notably, jGCaMP7b exhibited even more severe nuclear accumulation than other GCaMP variants, which may account for the nuclear jGCaMP7b evidenced in vivo (Dana et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by the N/C ratio data in Figure 1B and comparison with other variants.

claim: The total length and the complexity of neurites were significantly reduced in jGCaMP7b-expressing neurons.
source: Accordingly, the total length (Figure 1C) and the complexity (Figure 1D) of neurites were significantly reduced in jGCaMP7b-expressing neurons.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: Both cytosolic and nuclear versions of jGCaMP7-X have greatly enhanced the compatibility with neurons.
source: Depicted by neurite tracing (Figure 1A), both cytosolic and nuclear versions of jGCaMP7-X have greatly enhanced the compatibility with neurons.
evidence: This is supported by neurite tracing data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Neurons expressing jGCaMP7-X were essentially indistinguishable from GFP control neurons in neurite length and complexity.
source: In fact, neurons expressing jGCaMP7-X were essentially indistinguishable from GFP control neurons, in direct contrast to the neurons transfected with jGCaMP7 of the same amount of cDNA (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: jGCaMP7b significantly altered the major properties of CaV1.3 gating, with both inactivation and activation being enhanced.
source: jGCaMP7b significantly altered the major properties of CaV1.3 gating, that is, both inactivation and activation were enhanced (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: jGCaMP7b in HEK293 cells was expressed at the same levels as jGCaMP7b-XC or jGCaMP7b-XN when transiently transfected with the same amount of cDNA.
source: Demonstrated by both western blotting and immunohistochemistry, jGCaMP7b in HEK293 cells was expressed either in the cytosol or in the nucleus at the same levels as jGCaMP7b-XC or jGCaMP7b-XN, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: jGCaMP7 and jGCaMP7-X were at the same cytosolic or nuclear levels of expression when transiently transfected into neurons.
source: Likewise, jGCaMP7 and jGCaMP7-X were at the same cytosolic or nuclear levels of expression when transiently transfected into neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The total expression level of coexpressed jGCaMP7b-XC and jGCaMP7b-XN was even higher than that of jGCaMP7b.
source: Moreover, by coexpressing jGCaMP7b-XC and jGCaMP7b-XN, the total expression level estimated by immunostaining was even higher than that of jGCaMP7b, the latter of which caused significant damage to neurites whereas the total neurite length of jGCaMP7b-X neurons was about the same as GFP control neurons.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The expression levels of GCaMP-X versus GCaMP did not underlie their differential performances.
source: Therefore, the expression levels of GCaMP-X versus GCaMP did not underlie their differential performances.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the expression level comparison experiments.

claim: GCaMP bound CaV1.3 (α1D) at its apoCaM-binding domain whereas GCaMP-X was found to have no binding.
source: Notably, by coimmunoprecipitation GCaMP bound CaV1.3 (α1D) at its apoCaM-binding domain whereas GCaMP-X was found no binding (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Neurogranin bound GCaMP but not GCaMP-X.
source: Similarly, neurogranin, an important postsynaptic apoCaM-binding protein (Gerendasy and Sutcliffe, 1997), was unveiled to bind GCaMP but not GCaMP-X.
evidence: This is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: An optimal time window (OTW) for GCaMP-infected neurons of live mice is about 3–8 weeks postinjection.
source: In practice, an optimal time window (OTW) is about 3–8 weeks postinjection for GCaMP-infected neurons of live mice (Chen et al., 2013; Huber et al., 2012; Resendez et al., 2016), in order to achieve substantial levels of GCaMP expression and fluorescence but not too high levels prone to side-effects.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Nucleus-filling GCaMP was observed in a fraction of neurons 4–6 weeks postinjection, and the average N/C ratio was substantially increased when examined 8–13 weeks postinjection.
source: Consistently, by the criteria of N/C ratio (0.8), nucleus-filling GCaMP was observed in a fraction of neurons 4–6 weeks postinjection, and the average N/C ratio was substantially increased when examined 8–13 weeks postinjection (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: No neuron expressing GCaMP6m-XC fell into the nucleus-filled category even weeks beyond OTW (up to 13 weeks postinjection).
source: In direct contrast, no neuron expressing GCaMP6m-XC fell into the nucleus-filled category even weeks beyond OTW (up to 13 weeks postinjection).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Nucleus-filled neurons expressing GCaMP6m (N/C ratio >0.8) started to show less responsiveness than neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC as early as within OTW (4–6 weeks).
source: Here, nucleus-filled neurons expressing GCaMP6m (N/C ratio >0.8) started to show less responsiveness than neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC as early as within OTW (4–6 weeks) (Figure 2A), which may underlie the lower amplitude of Ca2+ responses (ΔF/F0) averaged over the whole population of neurons (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2A and 2C.

claim: Beyond OTW (8–13 weeks), GCaMP6m was more frequently and clearly found in the nucleus, and the neurons exhibited more significant differences from GCaMP6m-XC according to ΔF/F0, success rate, and SNR.
source: Beyond OTW (8–13 weeks), GCaMP6m was more frequently and clearly found in the nucleus, and the neurons exhibited more significant differences from GCaMP6m-XC according to all the three indices of ΔF/F0, success rate, and SNR.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: GCaMP-X outperformed GCaMP in imaging sensory-evoked Ca2+ dynamics especially beyond OTW.
source: GCaMP-X outperformed GCaMP in imaging sensory-evoked Ca2+ dynamics especially beyond OTW, which provides a simple but promising solution for long-term Ca2+ imaging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo imaging experiments comparing GCaMP and GCaMP-X.

claim: Slow Ca2+ oscillations have been observed from a variety of excitable or non-excitable cells.
source: Of note, slow Ca2+ oscillations have been observed from a variety of excitable or non-excitable cells (Uhlén and Fritz, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In neurons, oscillatory Ca2+ signals can increase the efficiency and specificity of gene expression.
source: In neurons, oscillatory Ca2+ signals can increase the efficiency and specificity of gene expression (Dolmetsch et al., 1998; Li et al., 1998), thus playing important role in neuronal functions, development, morphology, and even general health (Kamijo et al., 2018; Nicotera and Orrenius, 1998; Toth et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Oscillatory Ca2+ signals play an important role in neuronal functions, development, morphology, and general health.
source: In neurons, oscillatory Ca2+ signals can increase the efficiency and specificity of gene expression (Dolmetsch et al., 1998; Li et al., 1998), thus playing important role in neuronal functions, development, morphology, and even general health (Kamijo et al., 2018; Nicotera and Orrenius, 1998; Toth et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Spontaneous electrical activities are initiated at the early stage of neural development, and subsequently become more synchronized.
source: Spontaneous electrical activities are initiated at the early stage of neural development, and subsequently become more synchronized (Luhmann et al., 2016; Spitzer, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The frequency of Ca2+ fluctuation with GCaMP6m-XC was about 150 mHz during the first week, then gradually declined to the plateau around 20 mHz.
source: Statistical results demonstrated that the frequency of Ca2+ fluctuation with GCaMP6m-XC was about 150 mHz during the first week, then gradually declined to the plateau around 20 mHz (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The peak amplitude of Ca2+ oscillations exhibited a rising trend in neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC across the full term.
source: Meanwhile, the peak amplitude exhibited a rising trend in the neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC across the full term (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Both the frequency and the amplitude of Ca2+ oscillations acquired by GCaMP6m were drastically changed after DIV 17.
source: In contrast, both the frequency and the amplitude of Ca2+ oscillations acquired by GCaMP6m were drastically changed after DIV 17, and then even more deteriorated later in that the oscillation was less and less recognizable and eventually halted on DIV 28 (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: The comparison between GCaMP6m versus GCaMP6m-XC unveiled a crucial phase turning from increasing to decreasing synchronization around DIV 17–21 in GCaMP6m-expressing neurons.
source: As demonstrated by the temporal profiles of correlation coefficients, the comparison between GCaMP6m versus GCaMP6m-XC unveiled a crucial phase turning from increasing to decreasing synchronization around DIV 17–21 in GCaMP6m-expressing neurons (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) was aberrantly wider for GCaMP6m than GCaMP6m-XC, becoming noticeable on DIV 10, and much more pronounced (10-fold) later on.
source: Likewise, the full width at half maximum (FWHM), another index of oscillatory waveforms, was aberrantly wider for GCaMP6m than GCaMP6m-XC, becoming noticeable on DIV 10, and much more pronounced (10-fold) later on (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The distribution of frequency components started to change during DIV 10–17, when slow Ca2+ oscillations of 10–100 mHz appeared to be the dominant form.
source: The distribution of frequency components started to change during DIV 10–17, when slow Ca2+ oscillations of 10–100 mHz appeared to be the dominant form (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by FFT analysis data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The key parameters of Ca2+ dynamics measured by jGCaMP7b-XC were much closer to those by Fluo-4 AM than jGCaMP7b.
source: The key parameters of Ca2+ dynamics measured by jGCaMP7b-XC were much closer to those by Fluo-4 AM than jGCaMP7b, supporting that jGCaMP7b-XC is less toxic than jGCaMP7b.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC followed the typical development process of neonatal neurons, including neurite elongation/arborization and soma enlargement.
source: Indistinguishable from control neurons infected with GFP viruses (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC followed the typical development process of neonatal neurons, including neurite elongation/arborization and soma enlargement (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: These developmental processes were severely impaired by virally delivered GCaMP6m, especially after DIV 14 onwards.
source: In contrast, these developmental processes were severely impaired by virally delivered GCaMP6m, especially after DIV 14 onwards, when nuclear accumulation and neurite shortening became evident.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: At the early phase (before DIV 17), no significant difference between the two groups of GCaMP6m versus GCaMP6m-XC could be detected.
source: At the early phase (before DIV 17), no significant difference between the two groups of GCaMP6m versus GCaMP6m-XC could be detected.
evidence: This is supported by the temporal profile data in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: Toward the late stage (DIV 28 or later) of GCaMP-expressing neurons, the soma size was as small as ~200 μm2 in contrast to the neurons expressing GFP or GCaMP6m-XC (~300 μm2).
source: However, toward the late stage (DIV 28 or later) of GCaMP-expressing neurons, the soma size was as small as ~200 μm2 in contrast to the neurons expressing GFP or GCaMP6m-XC (~300 μm2), as confirmed by the statistical summary over three independent experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The oscillation amplitude linearly (R2 = 0.84) correlated with the neurite length in total.
source: Roughly, the oscillation amplitude linearly (R2 = 0.84) correlated with the neurite length in total (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The oscillation frequency and the total neurite length were inversely correlated (R2 = 0.99).
source: In direct contrast, the oscillation frequency and the total neurite length were inversely correlated (R2 = 0.99) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The level of synchrony (correlation coefficient) indicative of circuitry formation was positively correlated with the total neurite length (R2 = 0.86).
source: Resembling the amplitude, the level of synchrony (correlation coefficient) indicative of circuitry formation was positively correlated with the total neurite length (R2 = 0.86) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The frequency band of 10–100 mHz played a crucial role in Ca2+-dependent neuritogenesis.
source: According to the spectral analyses (Figure 3G, H), the frequency band of 10–100 mHz played a crucial role in Ca2+-dependent neuritogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FFT analysis data.

claim: The bell-shaped curves suggested that the relationships between Ca2+ oscillations and neuronal growth rates may depend on developmental stages, which reached the peak rates around DIV 10 for both neurite length and soma size.
source: The bell-shaped curves suggested that the relationships between Ca2+ oscillations and neuronal growth rates may depend on developmental stages, which reached the peak rates around DIV 10 for both neurite length and soma size.
evidence: This is supported by the growth rate analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 3 μl AAV-Syn-jGCaMP7b-XC (1.0 × 1012 v.g./ml) and 1 μl AAV-Syn-jGCaMP7b (1.0 × 1012 v.g./ml) led to similar levels of whole-cell expression.
source: 3 μl AAV-Syn-jGCaMP7b-XC (1.0 × 1012 v.g./ml) and 1 μl AAV-Syn-jGCaMP7b (1.0 × 1012 v.g./ml) led to the similar levels of whole-cell expression (the former would express much more in the cytosol).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: jGCaMP7b-XC was much less toxic than jGCaMP7b when comparing the indices of neuronal growth and Ca2+ oscillations.
source: Under such conditions, the results from the two groups of neurons were consistent with those with equal amounts/volumes of viruses. jGCaMP7b-XC was much less toxic than jGCaMP7b, by comparing the indices of neuronal growth and Ca2+ oscillations (Figure 4—figure supplement 4F), where neurite length and soma size of neurons expressing high-level jGCaMP7b-XC were nearly indistinguishable from GFP control neurons.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4F.

claim: Similar side-effects of jGCaMP7b in comparison with jGCaMP7b-XC were observed when viruses were added to cultured cortical neurons at the mature stage (DIV 21).
source: The viruses were added to cultured cortical neurons at the mature stage (DIV 21), which were subsequently examined to compare the effects of jGCaMP7b versus jGCaMP7b-XC (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). Analyses of both neurites and oscillations demonstrated similar side-effects of jGCaMP7b in comparison with jGCaMP7b-XC, starting to show up on DIV 28 and later on DIV 35 exhibiting significant differences in neurite length and oscillation characteristics.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Spontaneous Ca2+ activities in vivo are correlated to gene transcription and expression at the cellular and circuitry levels.
source: Similar to cultured neurons, spontaneous Ca2+ activities in vivo are also correlated to gene transcription and expression at the cellular and circuity levels (Laviv et al., 2020; Takahashi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The nucleus-filled neurons exhibited noticeable abnormalities in spontaneous Ca2+ activities even within OTW.
source: Similar to whisker deflection-response experiments in Figure 2, the nucleus-filled neurons exhibited noticeable abnormalities in spontaneous Ca2+ activities even within OTW.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Beyond OTW, nucleus-filling was often found from GCaMP6m while very rare from GCaMP6m-XC as indexed by N/C ratio.
source: Beyond OTW, nucleus-filling was often found from GCaMP6m while very rare from GCaMP6m-XC as indexed by N/C ratio (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: With GCaMP6m, the frequency and amplitude resulted in significantly lower values, accompanied by aberrantly wider FWHM and slower on/off rates.
source: With GCaMP6m, the frequency and amplitude resulted in significantly lower values, accompanied by aberrantly wider FWHM and slower on/off rates.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC maintained robust and stable spontaneous Ca2+ activities with key characteristics within the normal ranges across the full term of experiments (up to 11 weeks postinjection).
source: In contrast, neurons expressing GCaMP6m-XC maintained robust and stable spontaneous Ca2+ activities with key characteristics within the normal ranges across the full term of experiments (up to 11 weeks postinjection).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: GCaMP6m-XC significantly improved the SNR calculated from spontaneous Ca2+ signals in vivo, both within and beyond OTW.
source: Notably, GCaMP6m-XC significantly improved the SNR calculated from spontaneous Ca2+ signals in vivo, both within and beyond OTW (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Low-concentration injection of virus at 1 × 1011 v.g./ml exhibited extremely sparse expression of GCaMP6m and yielded a low cell count.
source: Low-concentration injection of virus at 1 × 1011 v.g./ml exhibited extremely sparse expression of GCaMP6m and yielded a low cell count.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The virus concentration, when increased to 5 × 1011 v.g./ml, resulted in a relatively larger number of healthy-looking cells expressing GCaMP6m.
source: The virus concentration, when increased to 5 × 1011 v.g./ml, resulted in a relatively larger number of healthy-looking cells expressing GCaMP6m. But the low image contrast still affected proper detection of Ca2+ signals due to neuropil fluorescence.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: High-expression levels of GCaMP (at the virus concentration of 1 × 1012 v.g./ml) significantly enhanced the fluorescence image contrast and greatly increased the numbers of GCaMP-positive cells.
source: High-expression levels of GCaMP (at the virus concentration of 1 × 1012 v.g./ml) significantly enhanced the fluorescence image contrast and greatly increased the numbers of GCaMP-positive cells. However, the majority of neurons exhibited severe nuclear accumulation, which would subsequently lead to aberrant Ca2+ dynamics and cell death (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: High-dose injection of GCaMP6m-XC virus at 1 × 1012 v.g./ml was beneficial for image contrast and the number of positive and healthy cells, while the N/C ratio remained within the low range.
source: In contrast, high-dose injection of GCaMP6m-XC virus at 1 × 1012 v.g./ml was beneficial for image contrast and the number of positive and healthy cells; meanwhile, the N/C ratio remained within the low range as expected.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Long-term, high-level expression of GCaMP6m-XC up to 92 days did not induce nuclear accumulation.
source: Most importantly, long-term, high-level expression of GCaMP6m-XC up to 92 days did not induce nuclear accumulation, whereas GCaMP6m at relatively lower concentration (1 × 1012 v.g./ml) already caused severe nuclear accumulation evidenced from 17 to 92 days (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The soma size of GCaMP6m-infected neurons was significantly smaller than that of GCaMP6m-XC from 55 to 92 days.
source: Meanwhile, the soma size of GCaMP6m-infected neurons was significantly smaller than that of GCaMP6m-XC from 55 to 92 days, presumably due to impaired spontaneous Ca2+ activities and related Ca2+ signals in these neurons.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Long-term (13 weeks) expression levels of AAV-Syn-GCaMP6m (at the concentrations of 5 × 1011 and 1 × 1012 v.g./ml) resulted in significantly lower expression levels than AAV-Syn-GCaMP6m-XC of higher concentration (1 × 1013 v.g./ml).
source: Long-term (13 weeks) expression levels of AAV-Syn-GCaMP6m (at the concentrations of 5 × 1011 and 1 × 1012 v.g./ml) in the brains of adult mice were quantified by anti-GFP immunofluorescence (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). And both dosages resulted in significantly lower expression levels than AAV-Syn-GCaMP6m-XC of higher concentration (1 × 1013 v.g./ml), excluding the expression level as the cause of less damage.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The soma size of neurons after long-term GCaMP-X expression was larger than GCaMP, while indistinguishable from the blank control neurons.
source: Of note, the soma size of neurons after long-term GCaMP-X expression was larger than GCaMP, while indistinguishable from the blank control neurons.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nuclear accumulation of GCaMP was readily discernible in 6-month-old Rasgrf2-2A-dCre;Ai148 mice.
source: Using confocal fluorescence microscopy, we examined GCaMP-expressing neurons from the layer II–III cortex of the 6-month-old Rasgrf2-2A-dCre;Ai148 mice (with TMP-inducible expression of GCaMP6f) (Figure 7A). Nuclear accumulation of GCaMP was readily discernible, although it was relatively less severe than long-term expression of viral GCaMP6m of high doses (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The complexity and length of neurites were reduced in Ai148 neurons as compared to GFP control neurons from DIV 21 onwards.
source: Neurite tracings indicated that the complexity and length of neurites were reduced in Ai148 neurons as compared to GFP control neurons from DIV 21 onwards (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The temporal profile of total neurite length indicated that neurite outgrowth was significantly slowed down or even halted on DIV 14 in Ai148 neurons in comparison with the control neurons.
source: The temporal profile of total neurite length indicated that neurite outgrowth was significantly slowed down or even halted on DIV 14, in comparison with the control neurons (GFP virus-infected and TMP treated) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: N/C ratio of GCaMP indicative of nuclear accumulation was gradually increased along with the expression time up to 1 month in Ai148 neurons.
source: Consistently, N/C ratio of GCaMP indicative of nuclear accumulation was gradually increased along with the expression time up to 1 month (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Ca2+ waveforms of lower amplitude were acquired from Ai148 neurons expressing nucleus-filled GCaMP across the full month than the nucleus-excluded subgroup.
source: Functionally, Ca2+ waveforms of lower amplitude were acquired from Ai148 neurons expressing nucleus-filled GCaMP across the full month than the nucleus-excluded subgroup (Figure 7F, G), consistent with the previous results by GCaMP plasmids and viruses that the side-effects would be exacerbated by nuclear GCaMP.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 7F and 7G.

claim: The major findings by virus-infected neurons are applicable to transgenic mice, where GCaMP expression is either TMP inducible or constitutive.
source: In summary, the major findings by virus-infected neurons are applicable to transgenic mice, where GCaMP expression is either TMP inducible or constitutive.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transgenic mouse experiments.

claim: Morphological and functional analyses strongly suggest that cortical neurons in transgenic GCaMP6 mice are also subject to GCaMP toxicity similar to virus-infected neurons.
source: Morphological and functional analyses strongly suggest that cortical neurons in transgenic GCaMP6 mice are also subject to GCaMP toxicity similar to virus-infected neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transgenic mouse experiments.

claim: GCaMP-X provides a viable solution for Ca2+ imaging applications involving long-time and/or high-level expression of Ca2+ probes.
source: In summary, GCaMP-X provides a viable solution for Ca2+ imaging applications involving long-time and/or high-level expression of Ca2+ probes.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by all the experimental data presented.
